intent: Remove missing Redis value keys from redis2 per-directory indexes during listing, while preserving directory-index membership when a value is concurrently recreated.

findings.suggested_fix: Ensure UpdateEntry restores its parent directory ZSET membership after writing, with the same super-large-directory handling as InsertEntry, or coordinate cleanup and update atomically.
findings.title: Concurrent UpdateEntry can leave a recreated entry unindexed
findings.why_it_matters: A directory has a stale member and no value. Listing reads the member, FindEntry returns ErrNotFound, and cleanup removes it; Exists observes no value and returns. A concurrent UpdateEntry then writes the value through doInsertEntry without adding the directory member. Future directory listings omit the live value until another operation restores membership.
findings.validation_reason: If the list's FindEntry misses, ZRem succeeds, Exists sees absence, and UpdateEntry's SET occurs afterward, the helper returns before the update and UpdateEntry calls only doInsertEntry without ZADD; this ordering is reachable from the inspected code, but incidence was not measured because no Redis-backed test or server was available.

findings.first_evidence: weed/filer/redis2/universal_redis_store.go:238 -- if err := store.Client.ZRem(ctx, dirListKey, fileName).Err(); err != nil {
findings.suggested_fix: Pipeline the ordered ZREM and EXISTS commands, then issue ZADDNX only when the existence check requires restoration; preserve recreation handling.
findings.title: Orphan cleanup adds sequential Redis round trips
findings.why_it_matters: Every missing value now incurs a ZREM followed by an EXISTS before the listing advances, adding two sequential Redis round trips per orphan on the first cleanup page. Directories with many expired entries can therefore have a substantially slower cleanup listing, even though later listings benefit from the smaller index. Consider reducing the per-orphan latency while preserving the recreation check.
findings.validation_reason: For a returned stale member whose ZRem succeeds, the listing loop synchronously waits for ZRem and then Exists before advancing, adding two sequential Redis commands on cleanup; this requires an orphan on the fetched page, and incidence/latency was not measured because no Redis-backed test or server was available.

findings.suggested_fix: Check the ZAddNX result and return or retry the repair failure through the listing path, preserving the store's error contract.
findings.title: Failed reindexing is silently ignored
findings.why_it_matters: If cleanup removed the member, then observes a recreated value, but the following ZAddNX fails, the helper discards the error and listing still succeeds. The live value can remain absent from the index and therefore invisible to later listings. Handle or expose the reindex failure so the caller can retry or report incomplete listing state.
findings.validation_reason: If ZRem succeeds, Exists sees the recreated value, and the subsequent ZAddNX fails, its returned error is discarded and the listing continues, so the repair failure is hidden; this command-failure condition is reachable in the inspected code, but incidence was not measured because no Redis-backed test or server was available.

triage_groups.title: Preserve directory index membership
triage_groups.context: Concurrent recreation and a failed repair can both leave a live value absent from the directory index.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Handle UpdateEntry membership and propagate or retry failed ZAddNX repair.
triage_groups.why: Both findings can make later listings omit a live entry, though they require separate fixes.

triage_groups.title: Limit orphan cleanup latency
triage_groups.context: Each missing member adds sequential Redis commands during listing.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Reduce per-orphan round trips while preserving the recreation check.
triage_groups.why: This is a separate listing-latency concern.

No test injects a Redis command failure during orphan repair, especially ZAddNX failing after a recreated value is observed.
